entries.rationale: fast-uri is a transitive dependency of ajv, reaching prod only through @cloudflare/tanstack-ai's LLM tool/response JSON-schema validation (and the shadcn build-time CLI, which is dev-only). The advisory (host confusion via a literal backslash authority delimiter) only matters when an untrusted URL is parsed with fast-uri to make a security/routing decision about its host — cubby never does that; ajv's uri-format check validates schema-shaped strings, not attacker-controlled hosts. Patched in >=3.1.4, but forcing that via a pnpm override triggers a full lockfile re-resolve that pulls in NEW critical advisories (seroval, effect), so the real fix is deferred to a dedicated dependency-bump PR where that churn can be reviewed in isolation.

brace-expansion DoS (unbounded expansion length -> OOM) requires an attacker-controlled glob/brace pattern. It reaches prod deps only via build-time tooling: @sentry/vite-plugin's glob (runs at build, patterns are our own) and the OTel GCP resource detector's transitive rimraf/glob (OTel is dev-only in cubby; production disables it per README). No runtime path feeds untrusted patterns to brace-expansion. Patched only in >=5.0.8 while minimatch consumers pin ^2.x, so a blanket override is a cross-major bump with lockfile churn — deferred to the same dedicated dependency-bump PR as GHSA-v2hh-gcrm-f6hx.

Follow-up to GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg: the same brace-expansion DoS, re-reported because the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation can be bypassed via unbounded intermediate arrays. Same module, same two prod paths, same analysis as that entry — @sentry/vite-plugin's glob (build-time, our own patterns) and the OTel GCP resource detector's transitive rimraf/glob (OTel is dev-only; production disables it per README). No runtime path feeds an attacker-controlled glob/brace pattern to brace-expansion, so the bypass changes reachability not at all. Patched in >=2.1.4 / >=5.0.9; still not overridable in isolation for the reason documented on the other two entries (forcing it re-resolves the lockfile and pulls in NEW critical advisories), so it is deferred to the same dedicated dependency-bump PR and shares their 2026-10-15 deadline. Published after this branch was cut and unrelated to it — it turned every PR in the repo red at once.
